title: Photo 030 · USSBBW · 자주요 흑유 척화 · 엎드린 자세 · 동아프리카 30대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a horizontal landscape-orientation photograph, 3:2 aspect ratio, wider than it is tall.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless mid-grey backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult East African woman in her late 30s, deep umber skin tone with a warm sheen, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, shoulder-length glossy curls, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears crescent-shaped earrings and has long nails with a chrome finish.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so long and vast that her head and her feet are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. An immense mass of soft heavy fat on her middle is squeezed out past her body on both sides where her weight presses it against the platform, spreading sideways into three or four heavy rounded folds with deep shadowed creases between them, the surface soft and uneven, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum. It merges seamlessly into her sides, her hips and her thighs with no boundary anywhere, one continuous body rather than a separate mass, not pregnant. A gigantic bust resting on the top fold, no waist at all, colossal hips more than three times the width of her shoulders and an enormous rounded rear, each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist, thick heavy calves, very thick upper arms, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body and her hands look small against her thighs. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it spreads sideways and presses flat against the platform beneath her.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Chinese Cizhou sgraffito ceramic style — a glossy jet-black glaze carved away to reveal bold cream-white peony scrolls and leafy vines, carved cream bands following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs like contour lines, dense leaf scrolls filling the space between every band. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Lying face down on the platform, her upper body propped up on both forearms with her elbows planted wide apart and her head raised and turned toward the camera, her legs straight and slightly apart, a colossal rear rising as two enormous rounded mounds far above the line of her back with a deep shadowed cleft between them, her broad heavy back built from massive horizontal rolls of soft flesh, her thighs flattening wide where they meet the platform, her body stretching across the full width of the frame from edge to edge.

Footwear: Extreme cream-white platform stiletto mules with a rounded toe, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the black glaze gleaming, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Horizontal 3:2 landscape-orientation full-body photograph, wider than it is tall.
